entities.summary: The Lutheran Church of the Redeemer is a Lutheran church in Jerusalem. It is a property of the Evangelical Jerusalem Foundation, one of the three foundations of the Evangelical Church in Germany (EKD) in the Holy Land. Built between 1893 and 1898 by the architect Paul Ferdinand Groth following the designs of Friedrich Adler, the Church of the Redeemer currently houses Lutheran congregations that worship in Arabic, German, Danish, and English. The Church, together with the adjoining provost building, is the seat of the Provost of the German Protestant Ministries in the Holy Land. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Lutheran Church of the Redeemer played a significant role in the religious landscape of Jerusalem during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, with its congregation serving as a hub for German-speaking Lutherans in the region. The church's establishment contributed to the growth of Evangelical Christianity in Germany and the Holy Land.
